clue.text: Don't say "confine"?

definitions.meaning: a curt command to stop talking, telling someone to say nothing more
to confine is to lock away or keep enclosed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb serves both as a rude order to be quiet and as a verb meaning to imprison or enclose.

clue.text: Fitter's the man to change — call in

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: in means the greeting goes inside the word for change

parts.note: to change is to alter
hi is a call or greeting

explanation.surface: A tradesman is told to change things by calling in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' looks like a tradesman, but it is the comparative of fit, and the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fitter means in better shape, the comparative of good health.

clue.text: Fat lot being drawn?

indicators.note: being, read with drawn, gives 'in tow', so the lot sits inside the pulling

parts.note: something drawn along is in tow
a lot is all, the whole amount

explanation.surface: A remark about a bulky amount being pulled along, or a lottery draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A lot being drawn is ALL in TOW. 'Fat lot' wants to be one phrase, as in 'a fat lot of good'; 'Fat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Any chips? I require one to make me 2

indicators.note: re-quire read as quire again: the letters are reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether chips are allowed and is told a doctor is needed to get well.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is a cross-reference to the answer at 2 down. The blog notes the anagram signal is weak; 'require' reads as re-quire.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician is a doctor, the one who makes a sick person healthier.

clue.text: Hospital with a fence sunk by Paddy Clarke

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a ha-ha is a sunken fence or ditch bounding a park, invisible from the house

explanation.surface: Someone is taken to hospital after Paddy Clarke tips them over a hidden garden fence.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy Clarke Ha Ha Ha is Roddy Doyle's Booker-winning novel, so the answer is what follows the boy's name in the title; 'with' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The full title of Roddy Doyle's 1993 novel completes the hero's name with this mocking laugh.

clue.text: What cross-country runners do to a boy?

definitions.meaning: cross-country runners are called harriers, so a jokey verb for what they do
a boy's name, the hero of the series this puzzle celebrates

explanation.definitionFit: Harrier runners do the joke verb, and the same word is a common boy's name.

clue.text: 5 down 25's friend has her way with 1

parts.note: the M1 motorway is a way, written MI
the figure one spelt out

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's friend gets her own way with somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1' looks like a reference to 1 across, but it is simply the number one spelt out. The M1 is England's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermione Granger is one of Harry Potter's two best friends in J K Rowling's books.

clue.text: Poem elevated characters one after another read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud tells us the phrase is heard, not spelled

parts.note: elevated means high, and people standing one after another form a queue

explanation.surface: Lofty letters in a poem are recited in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are people, not letters: people one after another make a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of seventeen syllables in three lines.

clue.text: 5 down 25's friend says one 14 is so distinguished

indicators.note: the clue signals that we hear the phrase spoken rather than read its spelling

parts.note: 14 down describes the weasel family; the old joke says a weasel is weasily (easily) recognised, so 'weasily' is how one is distinguished

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's friend has a reputation for being easy to pick out from the crowd of weasels.
explanation.walkthrough: The old riddle runs: a weasel is weasily recognised, a stoat is stoatally different (see 23). The made-up word 'weasily' sounds like the family name of Ron, Harry Potter's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Ron Weasley is Harry Potter's closest friend in J K Rowling's novels, so a friend of the boy wizard fits.

clue.text: Guardian man in sea came across advice for cyclist

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as 'we' in its editorials

indicators.note: in places the man inside the body of water

parts.note: the Aral Sea is in Central Asia
he is the pronoun for a man
to come across someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A Guardian journalist swimming in the sea met someone who told cyclists to protect their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian man' looks like one journalist but splits: a newspaper's editorials speak as 'we', and 'man' is the pronoun put into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety campaigns urge cyclists to protect their heads with protective headgear.

clue.text: Puts back on line when Larrie's off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or awry, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A train is put back on the track while a man called Larrie is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal: LARRIES rearranged; the apostrophe is ignored and its S is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A derailed train is returned to its track, its line, so it is put back on line.

clue.text: One pretending to detain players with pile-driver

indicators.note: detain means hold inside, so the players go within the pretender

parts.note: a shammer is one who shams or pretends
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: An impostor holds a group of players along with a heavy machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam hammer is a heavy power hammer, used for forging and driving piles.

clue.text: Power from the movies in writer, I reckon, means power to the psyche

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the run made by the others

parts.note: a writer is an author
to reckon is to figure, to calculate or suppose
Tyrone Power, the Hollywood star, was known as Ty Power

explanation.surface: A screen idol's power is set beside a novelist's musings about the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyrone Power was a 1930s-50s Hollywood leading man, so 'Power' is a surname, not strength; 'means' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a parent, teacher or boss who wields power over the mind is described by this phrase.

clue.text: A side's lost the war

parts.note: a cricket or football side is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
the possessive ending supplies its S

explanation.surface: A remark that one team or alliance was defeated in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: Germany, Italy and Japan formed the alliance that lost the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis powers were the coalition defeated in 1945, so a side that lost the war describes them.

clue.text: City sends meat on the bone back to Campbell

indicators.note: on puts the meat after the other pieces, as in a down entry
back tells us to read the bone's word in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rib is a bone
Sir Menzies Campbell, Liberal Democrat leader in 2007, was known as Ming
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A city returns a bone with meat on it to a man named Campbell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RIB to BIR. MING is the nickname of Sir Menzies Campbell, then leader of Britain's Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Birmingham in the English Midlands is a city, the second largest in Britain.

clue.text: Does the Eastern railway have to be such a beast?

parts.note: must means have to
a railway is a line

explanation.surface: Must a railway in the east be so beastly?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an adjective describing the weasel family, so 'such a beast' is a weasel-like one.
explanation.definitionFit: Musteline means belonging to the weasel family, like stoats, otters and badgers.

clue.text: Ally of 5 down 25 to retreat, being terribly bewitched

parts.note: Rubeus Hagrid, gamekeeper at Hogwarts, is Harry Potter's ally
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's friend retreats, frightened by witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Hag-ridden means tormented, as if ridden by a witch in the night, hence badly bewitched.

clue.text: Not many links here with home in small house

indicators.note: in places the home inside the small house

parts.note: a chalet is a small house, especially a wooden one
in means at home

explanation.surface: Few internet links are found at this home in a cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' sound like web links, but they are the rings of a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainlet is a small chain, so it has few links.

clue.text: Unrefined nature of organ — solver's special service (no air)

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
the clue addresses the solver as 'you', so the archaic 'yours' fits
the SAS is the Special Air Service; take out the air and its A, leaving SS

explanation.surface: A coarse character is attributed to an organ, a solver and a military unit without air.
explanation.walkthrough: THINE is the old form of 'yours'. The Special Air Service, Britain's special forces regiment, is the SAS; with 'air' removed, SS is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthiness is a coarse, down-to-earth quality, an unrefined nature lacking polish.

clue.text: A grain missing in city

indicators.note: missing tells us the named word is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: the city's letters appear at the start of these words only as a coincidence of the deletion; they come from removing the second word, not from a hidden run

explanation.surface: A single grain has gone missing somewhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes IN out of AGRAIN, leaving the letters of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in northern India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Second half of 18? On the contrary

definitions.text: Second half of 18? On the contrary

parts.words: Second half of 18? On the contrary
parts.note: the second half of the city at 18 is RA; on the contrary means the first half, AG, the chemical symbol of a precious metal

explanation.walkthrough: AG, the first half of AGRA, is the chemical symbol for this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ag is the chemical symbol of the precious white metal used in coins and jewellery.

clue.text: Royal Society, divided, enters saying (backwards) 950 = 1000, the Soviet view

indicators.note: enters says the split society goes into the saying, taking over its middle

parts.note: a maxim is a saying
the middle two letters of the word for a saying, the part the society's letters surround

indicators.note: divided says the society's two letters are split apart, with the middle of the saying between them

parts.note: RS is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's national academy of sciences
the same middle two letters, kept in place between the society's split letters

indicators.note: backwards tells us to read the number's spelling in reverse

parts.note: nine hundred and fifty written partly as words and partly in Roman numerals: NINE then L for fifty
the equals sign reads as 'is'
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A muddled statement of Soviet doctrine involving a learned society and some dubious arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided' and 'enters' put the R and S separately into the saying, one each side of its middle XI. The blog notes Araucaria writes 950 as NINE L, half words and half Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism-Leninism was the official ideology of the Soviet Union, its view of history and society.

clue.text: Quotient achieved by beast and 10

parts.note: a rat is a beast
10 is drawn as I and O, read as the letters

explanation.surface: A result is reached by an animal and a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotient is the result of dividing one number by another, a ratio.

clue.text: Official has permission more precious than 19

parts.note: may means is permitted to
gold, or in heraldry, is more precious than the metal at 19

explanation.surface: An official is allowed something more valuable than the metal next door.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, more valuable than the metal at 19.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the official who heads a town or city council.

clue.text: To agree with what's said in 8, another 14 is so different

definitions.text: with what's said in 8, another 14 is so different

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond, as accounts do

explanation.surface: A riddle about telling one member of the weasel family from another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition finishes the old joke begun in 8: a weasel is weasily recognised, and a stoat (another of the weasel family) is stoatally different.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke's punchline says the stoat is stoatally, that is completely, different, so the adverb is what it describes.

clue.text: Ivan the terrible meets the German who crosses the border

indicators.note: terrible suggests making a dreadful mess, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: der is the masculine form of 'the' in German

explanation.surface: Tsar Ivan the Terrible encounters a German who has just crossed the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the terrible' looks like the tsar's title but is the anagram signal: IVAN becomes INVA, then DER.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is one who enters another's territory by force, crossing its frontier.

clue.text: Craftsman with quiet 14

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
14 down describes the weasel family, of which the otter is a member

explanation.surface: A craftsman works alongside a silent member of the weasel family.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is a cross-reference to the weasel family; the otter is one. The answer also completes Harry's name at 5 down 25.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter is a craftsman who shapes clay into pots and other ceramics.

clue.text: Slip with message

parts.note: to slip is to make a mistake, to err
with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: A mistake is made along with a note sent to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to deliver a message or do a small task.
